title: National Consumer Credit Protection Amendment (Small Amount Credit Contract and Consumer Lease Reforms) Bill 2019 (No. 2)
short_title: National Consumer Credit Protection Amendment (Small Amount Credit Contract and Consumer Lease Reforms) Bill 2019 (No. 2)

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would overhaul rules for payday loans and rent-to-buy schemes.
It would introduce a cap on total payments under consumer leases, require equal repayments for small loans, and ban door-to-door sales of leases at homes.

The government says the bill implements most recommendations from a 2016 review and would allow regulations to cut the protected earnings limit for Centrelink recipients from 20% of gross income to 10% of net income.
changes: Introduce a cap on total payments under a consumer lease.
Require equal repayments and equal payment intervals for small amount credit contracts.
Remove the ability to charge monthly fees on the residual term of a loan when a consumer repays early.
Prevent lessors and credit assistance providers from selling consumer leases door-to-door at homes.
Introduce broad anti-avoidance protections for small amount credit contracts and consumer leases.
Strengthen penalties to increase compliance incentives.
summary.affected: Consumers taking out small amount credit contracts or consumer leases, and providers of those products.
